lines.en: What makes idioms so difficult is that their meaning rarely has anything to do with their words.
It is no use crying over spilled milk; what matters now is how we fix the situation.
Were I in your shoes, I would think twice before burning any bridges with the old team.
The plan seemed perfect on paper, but in practice it fell apart at the first sign of trouble.
Not until he was offered the job did he realize he had been sitting on the fence for months.
However busy she is, she always finds time to read, which shows where her heart really lies.
It is often the quiet employees who carry the team, though they rarely blow their own trumpet.
Little did we know that the quiet new colleague would turn out to be a blessing in disguise.
To be honest, the meeting was a waste of time; we spent an hour going around in circles.
Rarely does anyone hit the nail on the head as precisely as she did in that discussion.
Having invested so much already, they refused to pull out, which is a classic case of throwing good money after bad.
He tends to beat around the bush for an hour before he gets to the point, if he ever does.
When the truth finally came out, it turned out we had all been barking up the wrong tree.
It is pointless to flog a dead horse; the decision has been made and no argument will change it.
Were the two partners to bury the hatchet, the company would benefit enormously; as it stands, both are cutting off their nose to spite their face.
